links.outcome: Barriers to implementing CanRisk, including IT infrastructure and time burden
links.effect: IT infrastructure and time needed to complete the tool were main barriers; integration into existing IT infrastructure was recommended.
links.quote: The study has highlighted that future implementation activities should focus on reducing the time needed to complete a CanRisk calculation, integrating the CanRisk tool into existing IT infrastructure, and identifying appropriate contexts in which to conduct a CanRisk calculation.

links.outcome: Practitioner confidence and knowledge to use the risk tool
links.effect: Lack of confidence and knowledge was a main barrier; PCPs may benefit from CanRisk-specific training.
links.quote: PCPs may also benefit from information about cancer risk assessment and CanRisk-specific training.

screen.reason: Qualitative and vignette-based usability study evaluating the barriers and facilitators of implementing the CanRisk breast cancer risk prediction tool among primary care practitioners.
